title: apex-ayl.112 RED ratchet (msgw-caching-receipts F2 — the dominant claude-side cache invalidator) — one-request thinking retention: strip_thinking_blocks (ST/conversation/messages.rs:266; xli S-031 = codex-rs first-party parity) drops every non-latest assistant's thinking, so an assistant turn's signed thinking survives EXACTLY the next request then is stripped — pinning steady-state cache reads at the last pre-reasoning prefix every turn (receipts: corpus claude turns serve only 43.2% of input as reads despite 73-98% per-turn steady state). Three headless turns: t1/t2 each induce a thinking block (adaptive on by default for sonnet-5), t3 replies. In the t3 request the FIRST assistant message is messages[1] (fixed index: u1,a1,u2,a2,u3). Control pin (class model): in the t2 request, messages[1].content[0].type == 'thinking' — proves t1 thought AND the one-request retention replays it (if t1 did not reason, the probe is VACUOUS, never a false red). RED PIN: in the t3 request, messages[1].content[0].type == 'thinking' — t1's thinking SURVIVES INTO THE THIRD REQUEST, i.e. retention is extended beyond one request (the apex-ayl.108 decision: extended verbatim replay buys the 5m mid-prefix cache across turns; server-side alternatives clear_thinking_20251015 / block_binding:drop_block also live on this decision). Pre-cut FAILs: a1's thinking is stripped by t3, so content[0] is 'text'/'tool_use'. GREEN when the retention extension (or an equivalent server-side keep-window) lands. Anthropic permits replaying earlier thinking verbatim (text+signature pairs are immutable), so the GREEN state is API-legal.
